answer: Glacier-paced handle admission: each new agent identity must wait a slowly melting cooldown before its first outbound transaction, and the interval shrinks only with the account's own prior traffic. Sable accounts behind a single operator thus serialize instead of fanning out, because parallel registrations share one glacial clock. An attacker buying N identities pays N times the median wait, converting cheap mass signup into a costly wall-clock queue; onyx budget pools cannot compress it without genuine history. Cheap to enforce, expensive to rush.
